beliefs: Only the first character of a string is transformed; the rest is copied unchanged (abc→cbc, bcd→dcd, Hello→Jello) [E3, E4, E5]
Lowercase letters are shifted forward by 2 with wrap-around (a→c, z→b) [E2, E3, E6]
Uppercase letters are shifted forward by 2 with wrap-around (A→C, Z→B) [E1, E3, E6, E7]
Digits, punctuation, and non-space symbols are left unchanged [E1, E4, E5, E7]
A leading space is stripped (removed), and if the string is all spaces it becomes empty; the remaining string is then transformed on its new first character [E7, E8]
The empty string maps to itself [E7]
notes: E8 shows a leading space is dropped rather than kept: ' '→'', '   '→'', but ' a'→' a' (space removed, then 'a'... wait, output is ' a' with space kept). Actually ' a'→' a' keeps the space, so only an all-space or single-leading-space-with-no-letter case is stripped. Re-examining: ' '→'', '  '→'', '   '→'', but ' a'→' a', '  a'→'  a', ' x'→' x'. So spaces are stripped only when the string is entirely spaces. Updated rule: if the string consists only of spaces, return empty; otherwise transform the first character as before.
